title: Memory, Retrieval & Context Control
description: Study working-memory compaction, retrieval permissions and freshness, memory poisoning and provenance, and context budgeting by value. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Working-memory compaction
lessons.description: Define a must-preserve checklist for task summaries.
lessons.conceptOverview: Compaction should preserve goals, constraints, evidence references and unresolved decisions while removing redundant detail. Summaries are lossy; retain links to original artifacts for facts that may need verification.
lessons.whyItMatters: Critical constraints must survive context compaction.

lessons.title: Retrieval permissions and freshness
lessons.description: Trace authorization checks across retrieval and caching.
lessons.conceptOverview: Memory retrieval must enforce current access rights and freshness, not just embedding similarity. Revoked permissions and superseded records need to affect indexes and cached results.
lessons.whyItMatters: Memory access must reflect current permissions.

lessons.title: Memory poisoning and provenance
lessons.description: Specify which sources can update user preferences and how changes are audited.
lessons.conceptOverview: Untrusted documents can introduce misleading instructions or false facts into durable memory. Label origin, require appropriate confirmation for durable preferences and support correction or deletion.
lessons.whyItMatters: External claims cannot silently redefine user preferences.

lessons.title: Context budgeting by value
lessons.description: Propose a log filtering and evidence selection rule.
lessons.conceptOverview: A context budget should prioritize task constraints, recent relevant evidence and necessary tool outputs. Repeated logs and large irrelevant documents compete with useful information; retrieval must be selective.
lessons.whyItMatters: Context selection should preserve decision-relevant evidence.
